Buried in it is the best thing on the page — Stockhausen answering a CD-R handed over in an autograph line with a letter warning him off sixths and kitsch, and a flat prediction that he would end up scoring films.

issues.forecast: The strongest work on the field this week is not a launch — it is a syllabus. A month-long architecture studio in Accra, a film festival in its fifty-second summer, a label naming its mill on the garment tag: the transmission systems are outperforming the drops, and the reveal cycle is the only place heat is still running ahead of the work.
come_up: Pedagogy as the venue — studios and festivals out-transmitting launches
Provenance named on the object — mill, weave and deadstock on the label
São Paulo bass exporting itself instead of being sampled
decline: Pre-alpha teasers spending attention a build has not earned
Summit-stage group shows curated around a diplomatic theme
The single-city scene report — the hybrids are already two continents deep
issues.climate: Teaching over launching — the field is rewarding the institutions that hand something down, and discounting the reveal that has nothing to hand over yet.

entries.name: Nomadic African Studio 2026 — The New Non-Aligned
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club
entries.read: The African Futures Institute moved its studio to Accra for four weeks and pointed it at the 1950s Non-Aligned Movement — not as nostalgia, but as a working question about what autonomy looks like against digital empires and extractive economies. The framing is the part that lands: not utopia, not collapse, but speculative survival — how housing, labor, energy and ecology get made livable under pressure. Accra is the correct room for it. The city argued Pan-Africanism into being once already. Sitting through August 14, and almost nobody outside architecture knows it is happening.

entries.name: Newark Black Film Festival — 52nd Edition
entries.benchmark: Black Film Archive
entries.read: Fifty-two years. Screenings every Wednesday at the Newark Museum of Art, free, running to August 5. The longest-running Black film festival in the country has been doing the work since 1974 with a committee of volunteers and museum staff picking the slate, and it still travels almost entirely by word of mouth in Essex County. That is the tell. Institutions this old usually calcify or get bought; this one just kept programming. Free admission is not a marketing choice here — it is the thesis.

entries.name: badsista
entries.benchmark: Jim Legxacy
entries.read: The São Paulo DJ and BANDIDA co-founder is the one Brazilian producers name when asked who moved trap-bass into techno without it reading as a costume change. She has worked with Linn da Quebrada and Kelela; her catalog runs from ghetto-edit blends to the harder end of the club. São Paulo has been right about her for years — the gap is geographic, not qualitative. Baile funk is filling London rooms while most of the crowd cannot name a single producer, and she is the correction to that.

entries.name: AHABAN — Ajepomaa Design Gallery
entries.benchmark: Denim Tears
entries.read: Named for the Akan word for leaf. Handwoven Aso Oke, Fugu, organza and cotton batik cut from deadstock pulled out of GTP's mills in Accra — the material sourcing is not a sustainability footnote, it is the argument. Most houses working this lane say heritage and mean print. Ajepomaa names the weave, the mill and the origami pleating technique on the product page, which is the whole difference between a story and a receipt. Priced in cedis first, dollars second. That ordering matters.

entries.name: Project Override — Inuv8 Studios
entries.benchmark: Moonshots
entries.read: Ile-Ife is the right address for a game about a preservation unit waking up after 1,073 failed attempts to override the past — the Yoruba origin city building the archive-that-survives-collapse story is almost too neat. The ability framework, combat systems and narrative tooling are reportedly in. But this is a pre-alpha teaser with no platform, no window and an open call for publishers, and it has already collected more coverage than most shipped African titles get in a year. The lane is real. The read is early. Come back when there is a build.

issues.forecast: Three July releases, three running times: seven minutes out of Croydon on the 8th, twenty-seven out of Detroit on the 10th, seventy-eight out of a California state prison on the 17th. In the galleries the same arithmetic holds — ninety ceramics in Long Island City reading as a single argument, one beaded panel in San Francisco holding an entire migration. Compression is doing the work volume used to do. The long dump still charts; it just stopped meaning anything.
issues.climate: Compression over volume: the edit is where authorship now lives, and a release that refuses to end is telling on the room that let it run.
come_up: Fixed-length releases: 7 minutes, 27 minutes, no filler tax
Artist-owned imprints handling their own distribution — CHRRY, Street Certified
Hand-material archive work: raku clay, cowrie, Nymo thread
decline: The double album as proof of life
A chart debut mistaken for a verdict on the work
Weekly singles that exist to keep a catalog warm

entries.name: Akinsanya Kambon — Soul Sessions
entries.benchmark: PanAfrica lane — Project a Black Planet. Kambon's ceramics are the kind of object that show exists to argue for; he sits level with it, not beneath it.
entries.read: The title comes from Vietnam. Kambon served with the Marines from 1966 to 1968 as an infantryman and combat illustrator, and the soul sessions were weekly gatherings Black Marines organized to teach each other. He has been running some version of them ever since. He came home, joined the Sacramento chapter of the Black Panther Party as Lieutenant of Culture, and did layout and illustration for The Black Panther. Then thirty years teaching art at Cal State Long Beach, plus free youth programs out of his own studio. He is eighty. This is his first survey in New York. Over ninety figurative ceramics at SculptureCenter, made from the 1970s to now, fired in raku adapted with eucalyptus leaves and sawdust so the surfaces come out with a metallic sheen no kiln schedule can promise. The show is organized as seven sessions rather than seven decades: Thrones of Resistance, The Middle Passage, Rebellion and Uprising. Works on paper and archival material continue at CARA on West 13th, and the wall text tells you to take the E or F between the two. That instruction is the thesis. The room caught up in 2023 with the Hammer's Mohn Award; the work was finished long before the room arrived. Closes August 16.

entries.name: Bandgang Masoe — M.O.N.E.Y.
entries.benchmark: underground-rap lane — Chris Crack. Same instinct for the two-minute song as a finished thought rather than a sketch.
entries.read: Fourteen songs, twenty-seven minutes, forty-two seconds. Out July 10 on Street Certified Records, his third project of the year, and not one track overstays its welcome: Rent Due, Bread On My Mind, Don't Forget The Ricc, gone. Masoe has been in the BandGang orbit since the early-2010s Detroit run, and his most-played record is still Fuck a Baecation from 2018, a posse cut he shares with Babyface Ray, who left the lane and became a national name. Masoe stayed and kept the tempo. Twenty-two thousand monthly listeners against two million plays on an eight-year-old feature is the whole Detroit export economy in two numbers.

entries.name: Javan — Dare You/N2S
entries.benchmark: underground-rap lane — Jim Legxacy. South London, diasporic, auteur R&B; Javan is a few years back down the same road.
entries.read: Javan has settled on a release shape almost nobody uses any more: a double A-side, no album, no rollout, one drop roughly every ten weeks. Dare You/N2S arrived July 8 on his own CHRRY imprint — three songs, seven minutes — his third of 2026 after One More Shot and FATAL ATTRACTION/MAGIC. He was seventeen when Mixtape Madness handed him a Next Up? in June 2019, out of Croydon, and the seven years since have gone entirely into singles with no full-length attempted. The Instagram reads nine and a half thousand followers, seventeen posts, and a bio that says Let God. The gap is that the release discipline is already professional while the audience is still village-sized.

entries.name: Demetri Broxton — Ancestral Echoes: Crops of Empire
entries.benchmark: heritage-craft lane — Dame Atlas, Tamera. The material discipline rhymes; the object is a wall, not a product.
entries.read: Japanese glass beads, sequins, cowrie shells, recycled glass, 24-karat gold-plated brass, rayon chainette, wool, Nymo thread, serigraph on Japanese sateen cotton, goat-hair canvas, birch board. That is the material list for one panel, 59 by 29 inches. Broxton works from family photographs whose subjects were never named, tracing the move from the American South out to Oakland, and beads the gaps rather than filling them. MoAD's Salon gallery, 685 Mission Street, through August 16.

entries.name: Tory Lanez — Made You Think I Was Gone …But
entries.benchmark: underground-rap lane — Starlito is the nearest thing on the 50, and it isn't close: comparable output, opposite relationship to editing.
entries.read: No interviews, no festival dates, no press run, no artist in the building. The tenth album still opened at No. 35 with roughly 19,700 first-week units, which is a real fact about how distribution works in 2026 and the most interesting thing on offer here. Everything after that is arithmetic: 23 tracks, 78 minutes, split into a rap disc and an R&B disc, his second album of the year, released July 17 on his own One Umbrella from the California Men's Colony, where he is serving ten years for shooting Megan Thee Stallion. Volume is the argument because volume is the only thing available. The 50 rewards taste over reach; this is reach with the taste removed.

issues.forecast: What failed this week was enforcement, not taste: eight trade bodies proposed an AI label for streaming and left compliance to whoever volunteers, while the work that held its shape arrived in small signed units — 96 pages from Penguin, a 12HP module with an open SDK, one drum pattern six years deep. Authorship over announcement.
issues.climate: Authorship over announcement. Every object that cleared the gate tonight names a person you could write a letter to: a Chicago poet, a São Paulo producer, a four-person module shop, a designer who cuts her own knots. The loudest item on the board names a committee, and the committee made compliance optional.
come_up: Open-SDK instruments — Hermetic Modular on the Electrosmith Daisy
Brazilian 2-step and brime — CESRV, Speedtest, 2 STEP MAFIA BRASIL
Poetry as a $20 object — Penguin Poets' summer list
decline: Voluntary industry standards — the eight-body AI label
The AI download as a product — TIDAL delisting, Udio's walled garden
Debut campaigns with no mill behind them

entries.name: Phillip B. Williams — Lift Every Voice
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club
entries.read: Williams came up in Chicago, went through Cave Canem, and has spent a decade collecting the kind of prizes that usually pull a poet toward the lecture circuit: the Kate Tufts for Thief in the Interior, a Whiting, a Lambda, an American Book Award for Mutiny, then Ours in 2024, a novel-length act of conjure. Lift Every Voice goes the other way. It is short, and the compression is the achievement — three hours read aloud by the author. The poems set a mother who knew seven ways to say one word under her breath against a grandmother whose smile reflects the world, then land on what Williams calls the impossible lift of forgiveness. Nobody scores a book of poems on volume, which is why it takes the cover: the object is small, priced for anybody, answerable to no committee, and it will outlast every product announced this month. Penguin already has it flagged a best seller in pre-order, so the room is arriving. It has not arrived. Get there before the syllabi do. Published July 14 by Penguin Poets — 96 pages, $20.

entries.name: CESRV — BRIME!! / FRONT 2 DA BACK
entries.benchmark: Jim Legxacy
entries.read: Brime was never a crossover. When CESRV pressed BRIME! to vinyl in 2020 with Febem and Fleezus — the first Brazilian grime record on wax — the sleeve carried the 2012 Club World Cup final, Corinthians over Chelsea, and the argument was settled in the image before a bar landed: São Paulo was taking London's 140 and keeping it. Six years and one sequel later (BRIME!!, six tracks, April 1, Beatwise / EMPIRE) he surfaces on the 2 STEP MAFIA BRASIL compilation with "FRONT 2 DA BACK," pointing the tamborzão at American garage instead. The scene he started is now big enough for outsiders to file reports on. He is still the one moving the reference.

entries.name: Torishéju — When It Rains, It Pours
entries.benchmark: Denim Tears
entries.read: Boiled wool and duchesse satin, tied and bound until the knot distorts the body underneath it. Torishéju Dumi has shown since 2023 on deadstock and a Yoruba reference chain, and her first fall campaign puts both on film, Sølve Sundsbø shooting, Ellie-Grace Cummings styling. Apple helped pay for it, which is where the honest note goes: a debut campaign is a marketing object, not a collection, and the coats and cardigans revisiting Yorubaland dress are the part still standing in five years. The room is right about her. It got there on the clothes rather than the credits.

entries.name: Alchemy Lab — Hermetic Modular
entries.benchmark: Koala Sampler
entries.read: Most build-your-own-module ambition dies at the breadboard. Alchemy Lab is 12HP around an Electrosmith Daisy — 480 MHz, 64 MB of SDRAM — with six CV jacks fully exposed to an open-source hardware abstraction layer, 102 addressable LEDs, and a delay launching beside it that stretches to sixteen seconds. The detail that decides it: no price, no ship date. Platform first, product later.

entries.name: The AI Label — Eight Bodies, One Suggestion
entries.benchmark: Leveraging AI
entries.read: On July 10 eight organizations — the RIAA, IFPI, the Recording Academy, SAG-AFTRA, A2IM, WIN, IMPALA and the Human Artistry Campaign — proposed two streaming tags, AI-GENERATED and AI-ASSISTED, modelled on the explicit-content marker. Five days later TIDAL stopped paying royalties on tracks it reads as fully synthetic. One of those is a rule. The other is a suggestion, written that way on purpose: platforms opt in. So the same file can earn full royalties on one service, get demoted on the second and disappear from the third without a note changing. Note what it isn't: a floor. The independent artist this is meant to protect still has no answer on Spotify, and this week a man was due in a New York court over eight million dollars of streaming fraud that ran seven years before anyone stopped it. The disclosure conversation is loud and it is correct. The enforcement is a press release.

issues.forecast: Cape Town, Warsaw, a stretch of coast west of Accra: the three strongest rooms this week are all run by people who declined to let the market set the terms, and the strongest of the three belongs to a painter who builds work he has no intention of selling. Inheritance over invention.
issues.climate: Inheritance over invention. Everything that cleared the gate this morning points backwards on purpose: a Xhosa proverb used as a working method, a Ghanaian textile school named after what hands remember, a Nigerian curator seating a Polish abstractionist beside Ndebele geometry and Xhosa clay, a novelist who recorded the audiobook with her own daughter. The one entry asking to be judged on its narrative rather than its record is also the one furthest down the board.
come_up: Material as argument — cow dung and raw pigment on unprimed Belgian linen
Craft schools over brand incubators — Kokrobitey's fourth intake, Aug 16
Estates handing the keys to outside curators — Gierowski Foundation, Warsaw
decline: The comeback narrative as the product — press cycle outrunning the record
Novelty as a curatorial default
African material culture priced as spectacle

entries.name: Mawande Ka Zenzile — Indlela Ibuzwa Kwabaphambili
entries.benchmark: Lauren Halsey
entries.read: A river that never dries up, is never celebrated is cow dung and oil stick on unprimed Belgian linen, and the material is the thesis rather than the texture. Ka Zenzile has painted with dung for over a decade; what has changed at Stevenson Cape Town, where the show runs July 4 to August 15, is that he no longer uses it to argue against Western painting. He uses it as a knowledge system that was always sufficient on its own. He is also a practicing traditional healer, and he describes the studio in those terms: incense, pipe smoke, music, the rational mind quieted until a color flashes. His earlier paintings were representational and politically legible. These are intuitive, and harder to file. The detail that decides it: the show includes installations and interventions that cannot be bought, which he counts as artworks made for the audience's experience rather than for a wall. Inside a commercial gallery, inside a market that rewards African material as spectacle, that is a deliberate cost. Asked what he wants a visitor to leave with, he says art cannot be limited by what is fashionable. Fifteen August is the deadline and Cape Town is the only address.

entries.name: Valeria Luiselli — Beginning Middle End
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club
entries.read: A mother and a teenage daughter driving Sicily after a divorce. The audiobook is the tell. Luiselli reads it across eight hours with Maia Enrigue Luiselli, her own daughter, which turns a decade of accusations about autofiction into a production credit. Four generations of women, a grandmother's archaeological dig, migrants met on the roadside: this is the Lost Children Archive method turned on her own family line instead of somebody else's border. Publishers Weekly starred it. The room is correct here, and it took the room four novels to get correct. Published July 28 by Knopf — 368 pages, $35.

entries.name: Kokrobitey Institute — What Hands Remember
entries.benchmark: Material Culture
entries.read: The most useful institution in West African fashion this year is not a brand. It is a two-week workshop, 16 to August 30, at an institute the artist Renée Neblett founded in 1992 on the coast west of Accra. The fourth edition is titled What Hands Remember, and the faculty is the whole argument: practicing kente weavers and the textile scholar Seyram Agbleze sit alongside a Nigerian designer and the French designer Soline Charrier. Esi Otoo runs the Esi Sweater Project there, turning textile waste into handwoven garments and paid work for weaving communities. Earlier editions sent participants into Kantamanto market and the landfills behind it to source material. Curriculum, not campaign.

entries.name: Aether Commons — Azu Nwagbogu at the Gierowski Foundation
entries.benchmark: Project a Black Planet
entries.read: Warsaw is doing what Venice keeps announcing it will do. The Stefan Gierowski Foundation, set up in 2014 by the painter's family to look after his estate, handed the reinterpretation of that estate to Azu Nwagbogu, the Lagos curator behind LagosPhoto and the African Artists' Foundation. Twenty works, eleven artists, running May 31 to October 18 at plac Dąbrowskiego 8/11. Gierowski's canvases are distributed through the rooms as gravitational centers rather than historical anchors: a 1975 geometric painting set against Esther Mahlangu's Ndebele fields, late oils against Mona Hatoum's marbles, Andile Dyalvane and Zizipho Poswa's clay in the same argument as Olafur Eliasson's light. The claim is not that abstraction was secretly African. It is that light was never anybody's property. An estate letting an outside curator rewrite it is rarer than any single object in the room.

entries.name: Young M.A — KWEEN
entries.benchmark: Starlito
entries.read: Fifteen tracks, independent, May 29, a decade after “OOOUUU.” The FADER got her on the record on July 22 and the interview is sharper than the album: a bottle a day, a 2023 hospitalization for liver complications, and “Hennessy Medusa” as the one track where the writing catches the life. Sobriety is not a genre. The record made from the far side of it is the one worth waiting for.

issues.forecast: The sharpest account of the street economy published this year came from a legal scholar with footnotes, and two of the rappers on this board are narrating the same transaction from inside it. Capture over reform.
issues.climate: Capture over reform. Kojo Koram's question is who owns a criminalized economy once it goes legal, and the answer he finds across five continents is whoever already owned everything else. Read the rest of the board against that: two independent rappers building catalogs at a pace no label would fund, a self-taught artist in Los Angeles who took the most commodified cloth in America and treated it as a surface rather than a garment, and a two-person show in Sharjah paid for by the institution hanging it. Ownership is the only story here that is genuinely current.
come_up: Reportage over polemic — five continents, no thesis defended in advance
Commissioned over rented — Sharjah funding the work it hangs
The cloth as the surface, not the logo — denim artistry out of Los Angeles
decline: Release cadence as a substitute for a record
Shock titling as a growth strategy
Legalization read as justice

entries.name: Kojo Koram — The Next Fix
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club
entries.read: Angola, Louisiana: a plantation that became a prison, and the first stop on a reporting trip that ends with Silicon Valley selling psilocybin as a wellness category. Koram crossed five continents to ask one question, and it is a property question rather than a moral one. When a criminalized substance is rebranded as a commodity, who is standing there to collect? He is a legal scholar, born in Accra and raised on Merseyside, and his first book, Uncommon Wealth, took the English PEN Hessell-Tiltman Prize and an Orwell shortlist for arguing that Britain's post-imperial economy was built by lawyers more than by statesmen. Same method here. Dispensaries now sell the thing that carried life sentences, and the sentences have not been unwound. He refuses the easy version and says so on the jacket: not a polemic for or against legalization. Note what it isn't: a reform story with an ending. Akala calls the case irrefutable. Koram has worked the podcast circuit all month, This Is Hell! on July 28, which is most of the reason a Verso title is moving at all. Published July 28 by Verso in the US — 304 pages, $29.95; the British edition landed June 4 from John Murray.

entries.name: Body Quotidian — Laila Majid & Inaam Zafar
entries.benchmark: The Shed
entries.read: A misted bathroom mirror, UV-printed, that only completes itself once you stand in front of it. That is Laila Majid's Steam 07, 2026, and it hangs in Gallery 6 at Al Mureijah Square until September 20 beside Inaam Zafar's Mourners. Majid works out of London and shows with Niru Ratnam; Zafar works out of Lahore and shows with Gray Noise. Raja'a Khalid, an assistant curator, put the two of them in one room and let the proximity carry the argument: latex partitions and cat-toy tinsel on one wall, figuration dissolving into grief on the other. Sharjah commissioned Zafar's pieces rather than borrowing them, and entry costs nothing. That ordering matters.

entries.name: Janett Kabeh
entries.benchmark: Denim Tears
entries.read: Denim is the most over-explained cloth in America and the least often treated as a surface. Kabeh, self-taught, based in Los Angeles, came out of fashion design and went sideways into it: stitch as mark-making, pointillism in indigo, silhouettes built from hues of blue rather than printed onto them. She describes the subject as human touch and nostalgic eras, which reads soft until you notice she is making pictures out of the fabric itself rather than pictures on it. The public record is thin, and that is the honest part of this number: an Artsy listing, no dated survey, no institution behind her yet. Downtown Los Angeles opened an 11,000 square-foot Denim Institute Museum in June to enshrine 25 brands. The more interesting work is a few miles away, one person and a needle.

entries.name: Meechi Mono — Whoever Listens
entries.benchmark: Showly
entries.read: 63,719 monthly listeners, one album deep. Broward County, and the register is the post-Gen-Z one: melodic, aggrieved, closer to confession than to flex. Debut single Blocklist landed July 11 last year; The Viewing has done 614,000 plays with no press cycle behind it. Whoever Listens is the first full statement, and Rita followed it. Early, unproven, moving on its own steam.

entries.name: King Hendrick$ — Mob America 2
entries.benchmark: Chris Crack
entries.read: Leaving the Lot has 43.4 million plays and earns them; the man can build a hook that sounds like a parking lot at two in the morning. There is real lineage here too. Building Castles on Black Sand got a ChopNotSlop edition this year, which places him inside the DJ Screw succession rather than next to it, and that is a craft decision most rappers at 364,000 monthly listeners would not bother to make. The problem is the count. Eight projects across 2024 and 2025, then Mob America 2 and Rari Pedal this year, is a supply schedule rather than a discography, and a song titled Anne Frank is reach dressed as edge. The screw remix proves he knows what a record is. Nothing else on the release calendar behaves like it.

issues.forecast: A reed that Senegalese farmers pay to clear out of the river is now the insulation in Dakar's best new walls, and almost everything strong on this board was built from something already lying around. Reclamation over import.
issues.climate: Reclamation over import. Worofila's answer to a concrete city is a weed nobody wanted and soil dug from the site; Shannon Sanders' answer to the American family novel is a deed and four dead relatives who will not stop talking; DJ Doggo's answer to the UK garage revival is to produce it in Lisbon and press it in Rio rather than shipping it back to London. Read the counter-read the same way. Locarno is showing thirteen African films and 233 films in total, and that ratio is the festival's actual position on the continent, whatever the press release says. What looks weak this week is anything that had to be bought in.
come_up: Compressed earth and typha written as a spec, not a gesture
Catalog numbers over rollouts: Lisbon produces, Rio presses
The ancestor as narrator and the deed as the plot
decline: The regional strand standing in for a program
Concrete's borrowed prestige
Earth building filed under nostalgia

entries.name: Worofila
entries.benchmark: Lauren Halsey — an argument made in the material of the place, at building scale
entries.read: Typha is a cattail that has choked the Senegal River valley for decades, a green tide farmers pay to clear. Worofila weaves it into wall panels, lays it into ceiling mats and mixes it into adobe, because the stem is honeycombed with air and insulates better than most of what gets imported. The Dakar practice, founded in 2019 by Nzinga B. Mboup and Nicolas Rondet and named for the Fann-Hock street where its office sits, builds in compressed earth blocks in a city that wears a concrete skin. Facades step out in fine horizontal ridges so each course throws a blade of shade onto the one below it: the building cools itself with geometry and nothing else. The portfolio is not boutique. Houses at Sendou and Ngor, sixteen stations on Dakar's regional rail line, an eco-pavilion for the environment ministry, and the earth work on Kéré's Goethe-Institut Dakar, which opened April 18. Mboup trained in Pretoria, passed through Adjaye Associates, and co-authored two studies of how Dakar actually houses itself. Next comes a gallery in Benin City raised in the Benin Kingdom's cob technique and a training center at Sebikotane, so the method leaves the studio. That ordering matters.

entries.name: The Great Wherever — Shannon Sanders
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club — the same insistence that the reading is about land, money and who kept the receipts
entries.read: Four ghosts narrate the parts of the story the living have agreed to forget. Sanders' first novel turns on a deed: a Tennessee farm bought by Thomas Lamb, one of the first Black landowners in his community, inherited a century later by a thirty-two-year-old gig worker in Washington with debt to clear. The room caught this one correctly. Starred reviews at Kirkus, Publishers Weekly and Booklist, a Book of the Month pick, summer lists at NPR, Esquire and People. What earns it is the voice rather than the premise. The dead are petty, funny and specific, passing judgment on romantic and sartorial decisions alike, which is exactly what keeps an inheritance saga from setting into a thesis. Published July 7 by Henry Holt — 416 pages.

entries.name: DJ Doggo — Ésselou / Latido Ao Luar
entries.benchmark: Jim Legxacy — the same splice instinct, minus the songs; Doggo works instrumental and lets the drum carry the argument
entries.read: Two tracks, catalog 40FM096, out November 12, 2025 on the Rio label 40% Foda/Maneiríssimo. Diogo Vasconcelos produces from Lisbon and presses in Brazil, which is the whole idea: the garage shuffle travels south, the funk drum comes back north, and neither end is the guest. Bandcamp's July 23 scene report finally put the axis on the record. Almost nobody outside it has looked yet.

entries.name: Open Doors Screenings 2026 — Locarno
entries.benchmark: Black Film Archive — which does the same curatorial work permanently, without needing a host festival's calendar
entries.read: The strand itself is genuinely programmed, which is what makes the arithmetic sting. Delphine Jeanneret and Ibee Ndaw have assembled thirteen films from twelve African countries for Locarno's 79th edition, 5 to August 15, mixing fiction, documentary and hybrid work and asking to be sat with rather than sampled; the world premiere of Aymar Esse's La kora de mon père and the Swiss premiere of Ique Langa's The Prophet are in it. Then the numbers. Locarno is running 233 films from 69 countries with 103 world premieres, and the Piazza Grande belongs to Olivia Wilde and James Gray. A continent-wide focus that fits inside a sidebar is a focus a festival can quietly drop next August.

entries.name: Chapter 3 — Vanessa Lee
entries.benchmark: LAAMS — a small room that functions as infrastructure for a neighborhood rather than a destination for visitors
entries.read: 4512 Third Street, Bayview, between La Salle Avenue and Third. Vanessa Lee, who already runs Smoke Soul Kitchen, has filed to open Chapter 3 there: a bookstore and cafe in a district that has spent years with the Linda Brooks-Burton Library as its only dependable source of books. Lee went to school in the Fillmore, a five-minute walk from Marcus Books, and that lineage is not decoration. Chapter 3 is one of nine Bayview storefronts funded this year through the city's Storefront Opportunity Grants, arriving just after a Renaissance Entrepreneurship Center and Harvard Business School study of the Third Street corridor recommended precisely this. A permit is not a ribbon. Come back when the door opens.

issues.forecast: What failed this week failed politely. Nina Protocol spent five years telling independent artists they could own their distribution, moved fifty thousand dollars in total, and was folded into SoundCloud on July 22 with the rails left behind. Everything that held up on this board arrived with its teeth already out. Friction over finish.
issues.climate: Friction over finish. dälek have been making the same argument out of Newark since 1998 and the eighth album states it in forty minutes without a single soft edge; Taring Padi have been printing that argument onto banners out of Yogyakarta since 1998 and hung thirty years of them in a Fitzrovia townhouse this month; Michelle Santiago Cortés spent an essay establishing that research without a verification step is just taste with a bibliography attached. Read the bottom of the board the same way. A book with the sharpest subject in the room arrives wrapped in a healing-journey register, and a platform built on artist ownership got acquired for its writing rather than for its artists. The work that kept an edge on it is the work that survived contact.
come_up: Records that argue: Ipecac's only rap act, eight tracks, no soft landings
The archive as the asset — SoundCloud bought Nina's criticism, not its rails
Woodcut and cardboard as distribution: the workshops, not the wall labels
decline: Artist ownership pitched as a deck rather than built as a business
The healing frame bolted onto a structural argument
Research with the accountability step quietly removed

entries.name: dälek — Brilliance of a Falling Moon
entries.benchmark: Chris Crack — the nearest thing on the 50, though dälek predate the lane by two decades
entries.read: Track six is called I AM A MAN, which is the placard Memphis sanitation workers carried in 1968, and Will Brooks never explains the reference because the record assumes you already have it. Eight tracks, forty minutes, out March 27 on Ipecac as IPC295LP: the eighth dälek album and the leanest, cut at Deadverse Studios across 2024 and 2025, mastered by Alan Douches at West West Side. Brooks and Mike Mare build it from dust-caked breaks, Wu-era strings and a wall of guitar feedback that never resolves, and the title is lifted from Erik Larson's account of Berlin before the war. Two things make it the record of this board rather than a good noise-rap album. dälek have done this from Newark since 1998, which makes them the ancestor of a lane that mostly does not know it has one. And they remain the only hip-hop act on a roster built for noise rock, so the aggression here is structural rather than borrowed. A June vinyl variant ran to 300 worldwide. The gap is that a catalog this deep is still priced like a curiosity.

entries.name: Michelle Santiago Cortés — The End of Research
entries.benchmark: Free Game — the same gatekeeping instinct, turned on the people who borrowed the word
entries.read: OpenAI now sells a half-zip with the word Research embroidered on it in cursive. Santiago Cortés puts that merch drop at the center of an argument about what the word has come to mean: moodboards, to-be-read lists, TikToks inviting you to spend a research day with someone, a whole leisure economy that borrowed academia's prestige and left the verification behind. Published July 24 in ArtReview. The sharpest turn is on artists, who she places awkwardly close to the scene of the crime once the accountability question is raised, since art has no protocols for verifying anything. It ends where the argument should start: nothing worth calling research survives without a little friction.

entries.name: Taring Padi — Rakyat Pasti Menang
entries.benchmark: Lauren Halsey — community-authored work built to leave the gallery, here at protest scale
entries.read: 93 Mortimer Street, London W1W 7SS, Wednesday to Sunday, eleven until six, running to November 22. Ibraaz has given its Majlis over to nearly thirty years of banners from a collective founded by art students in Yogyakarta in 1998, in the months after Suharto fell. The title translates as the people united will never be defeated, and the display rotates rather than sitting still, which is the correct way to hang objects built to be carried. The workshops are the actual program: cardboard puppetry on July 11, woodcut printing on July 12, both taught by the collective, because the whole method is reproducible by design. Taring Padi left documenta fifteen in 2022 with more than a thousand puppets and a banner removed over antisemitic imagery, for which they apologized. A thirty-year archive is not a clean object, and hanging it as though it were would have been the cowardly version.

entries.name: Dr. Sarah L. Webb — Colorism
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club — nearest on the 50 by subject, and nothing like it in register
entries.read: Webb has run the Colorism Healing platform for years and the ground covered here is wider than the discourse allows: dating and pop culture, yes, but also access to education, work, social services and politics, across communities of color and white communities alike. The subject is a blade. The packaging is a healing journey. Only one of those two things travels. Published July 7 by Legacy Lit — 256 pages, $18.99.

entries.name: Nina Protocol — The SoundCloud Migration
entries.benchmark: Untitled Stream — the closest thing on the 50 to what Nina was trying to be
entries.read: Nina said it would be profitable if it ever reached ten percent of Bandcamp's daily volume. Components ran the arithmetic in July: fifty thousand dollars spent on Nina across its entire five-year life, against a hundred and fifty-one million on Bandcamp in 2025 alone. The platform went dark on July 15; SoundCloud announced the acquisition on July 22, terms undisclosed. Read what actually changed hands. Not the Solana marketplace, not the Arweave storage, not the team: the editorial archive and the genre map, which is to say the writing. Nina's most valuable product turned out to be its criticism, and it took a shutdown and a sale to establish that. Migrating artists get a free subscription until December.

issues.forecast: Accra spent this month building the institution London keeps convening panels about. Manju Journal, nine years a magazine, filed a nonprofit arm on July 7 and put a two-day textile workshop on the calendar for August 20; the fund follows in 2027. The same instinct runs the length of this board. A Detroit rapper releases sixteen tracks with one guest on them. A Los Angeles singer spends the film budget on the song nobody streamed. Ownership over placement.
issues.climate: Ownership over placement. Every entry here is holding onto a piece of the process that the industry standard says to outsource. Iman Europe financed a short film for the album cut with twenty-six thousand plays instead of the one with 1.6 million, which is a decision about what an album is for. BandGang Lonnie Bands put out a sixteen-track record with a single feature on it, in a scene where the guest list is the marketing plan. Richmond Orlando Mensah turned a publication into a funder rather than waiting for a Western foundation to notice Accra. Read the bottom of the board against that. Ian Woods still cuts every piece by hand with a blade, and the hand is now aimed at Olympic sportswear and the most photographed faces alive, which is the one place on this board where the method outruns the subject. The measure this week is not who got the placement. It is who kept the thing after the placement was over.
come_up: The deep cut as the single: filming the 26,000-play song, not the 1.6-million one
Publications filing as institutions — Manju's July 7 conversion is the template
One guest across sixteen tracks: the record that doesn't rent an audience
decline: Placement as a career: the feature verse that outstreams your own catalog forty to one
A gatekept method pointed at the most reproduced images on earth
Press for the scene with no structure underneath it

entries.name: Iman Europe — Ego Death (The Official Short Film)
entries.benchmark: Baby Rose — nearest on the 50 by voice and independence, though Iman Europe owns the release apparatus outright
entries.read: Iman Europe has a song with 1.6 million Spotify plays. She spent the film budget on one with 26,634. Ego Death is track five on Chrysalis, out September 19, 2025 on Good Soil Productions: fifteen tracks, every one of them built with Kaelin Ellis, which makes it a record rather than a folder of singles. The short film went up on her YouTube in the last week of July; Stanisland wrote it up on the 29th. Her own framing is a question about who wins between the ego and the self, and the film answers it rather than decorating the track. Nothing in the streaming math recommends any of this, and she knows that math better than most: she ran artist relations at Sound.xyz before going independent. Doing it anyway is the argument that an album is a body of work, not a container for the one song that traveled. Come back in November and see whether the film moved the number.

entries.name: Djamel White — All Them Dogs
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club is the nearest thing on the 50, and it isn't close; the 50 carries no literary-fiction lane at all
entries.read: A six-way auction behind it. Tony Ward comes back to West Dublin after five years away, takes work under an enforcer called Flute Walsh, and finds the pull is not toward the job. White is 28, managed a tattoo shop, lives in Lucan where the book is set, and grew the novel out of a short story written in the first lockdown. The Booker longlisted it on July 28 from 163 submissions and he is the youngest name on the list. Note what carries it: not the plot, which is standard gangland, but the vernacular, handled with enough precision that the judges led on the dialogue rather than the violence. Publishes March 26, 2026 by John Murray — 240 pages.

entries.name: New Africa Cultural Initiative
entries.benchmark: Black Film Archive — the same move, one person's archive hardening into an institution
entries.read: Manju Journal spent nine years documenting Ghanaian and pan-African creative work. On July 7 it filed a nonprofit arm and started programming instead. First cohort: 20 and August 21 in Accra at the Foundation for Contemporary Art, Zohra Opoku leading on textiles and archival photography, her first time running one. Lagos in October, Dakar in November, Abidjan in December. The unrestricted fund is promised for 2027, which is the part to check.

entries.name: BandGang Lonnie Bands — Motor City Slicker
entries.benchmark: Starlito — the same independent arithmetic, run over a decade and a half
entries.read: Sixteen tracks, forty-two minutes, one feature. KEY! turns up on Super Fancy and nobody else turns up at all, which on a 2026 Detroit rap album is close to a policy statement. Out April 29 on Antimedia and Roundvalley through Create Music Group. Delante Landrum has been doing this since he was thirteen, when BandGang formed around Six Mile Bronx on the west side, and the titles still read like a ledger: Det Blues, Detroit River pt 2, Charge It To The Game, Skeechy Lil Artist. The gap is in the streaming column. His biggest song by a distance is Homicide, where he is a guest on somebody else's record, at nearly 25 million plays; the cuts on this album sit in the low thousands. The catalog he owns is the one nobody counts.

entries.name: Ian Woods
entries.benchmark: Robert Gallardo — the exact neighbour: Instagram-built, collage-rooted, working the seam between art and commerce
entries.read: The method has not changed since 2020 and the method is the whole argument: two printed images stacked, a pattern drawn on the top sheet, an X-Acto blade through both, glue, and a face that reads as two faces at once. Illinois born, Dallas raised, working out of Palm Bay. The New York Times Book Review put his jacket for Elias Canetti's I Want to Keep Smashing Myself Until I Am Whole, designed by Alex Merto at Picador, among the best covers of 2022. His project list now opens with Nike's Winter Olympics, Neymar's PUMA Future 9s, Shinola and the Jordan AJ40. The blade is gatekept. What it cuts is the most reproduced imagery on earth, and that is where the score settles.

issues.forecast: The only finished object on this board is a dress. Everything else is advance work: 106 seconds ahead of an album called Starlife, sixteen compiled tracks ahead of a debut called OSSHLAND, one viral record ahead of a catalog, a browser beta at 69 pounds ahead of a plugin due in the fourth quarter. Finished small over promised large.
issues.climate: Finished small over promised large. Four of these five are advance work for something that has not shipped, so the read is which fragment stands up alone. Surf7's GOOSE COAT has 3.09 million Spotify plays and his next-biggest song has 252,000, which is a hit rather than a catalog. Victony issued SLICK on his own OUTLAWVILLE imprint, licensed out rather than signed away, and then filled it with 106 seconds. Black Fortune spent nine months building Osshland into a vocabulary his audience actually speaks and still has not released the album it points at. Tim Exile discontinued one modular system in April and sold version 0.1 of its replacement in July, with the usable build promised for the fourth quarter. Against all of that, an Accra atelier cut a whole collection out of mill offcuts and hung it on a rail. It can be bought, worn and judged today, which this week is the rarer achievement.
come_up: Mill deadstock cut as the good cloth rather than the compromise
Own-imprint releases: licensing distribution out instead of signing yourself in
Builders leaving the big host to own their own stack
decline: The 106-second single working as an album announcement
One song at 3.09 million plays and the catalog at a twelfth of it
Version 0.1 sold at full intent while the finished build waits on a quarter

entries.name: Ajepomaa Gallery — AHABAN
entries.benchmark: diasporic-fashion lane, nearest is Derschutze; the material discipline runs closer to Tamera
entries.read: The cloth starts as mill offcuts. AHABAN, named for the Akan word for leaf and built around what is left of Ghana's forests and waterways, is cut from handwoven Aso Oke and Fugu alongside cotton batik made from deadstock sourced out of GTP's mills, which puts the collection's material story in a warehouse most designers write off. The convention in luxury is to treat deadstock as a limitation and say so in the press release. Ajepomaa Mensah treats it as the good cloth and spends the hours on construction instead: knife, box, bias and sunburst pleats, origami folds worked into a batik that was never engineered to hold a shape. She has run the house out of Accra since February 2010 and sells it from 53 Adjiringano Road, from ₵1,288 for the Kenya top to ₵3,888 for the Halima dress, shipping free inside Ghana. Sixteen years in one city, no runway theatrics, and a rail of finished garments you can buy this afternoon.

entries.name: Victony — SLICK
entries.benchmark: already on the 50 in the global-diaspora lane; the honest test inside it is Baby Rose
entries.read: One minute forty-six seconds. SLICK landed on July 8 with the phonogram line reading OUTLAWVILLE, Victony's own imprint, and Encore holding the license, which is a more interesting sentence than the song: at twenty-five, four years after Soweto made him portable, he is renting distribution rather than being absorbed by it. Ozedikus and Dera The Boy build the track from electronic texture over loose live percussion and leave the voice on top with nothing to fight. An influencer, Amma, opens it. It is well made and it is thin, a mood sustained for the length of a lift ride, and its job is to keep Starlife warm next to FRE$H. He is already in the 50. This is not the record that tests the seat.

entries.name: Black Fortune — Road To Osshland: The Series
entries.benchmark: underground-rap lane, nearest in method is Chris Crack, who built a country out of a catalog with no major behind him
entries.read: Osshland was a vocabulary before it was a place. Black Fortune, out of Landover, Maryland, has been extending the OSSH lexicon since OsshWop in 2018, through a near-fatal stabbing and the record he made after it, and on May 8 he compiled the four Road To Osshland EPs into a sixteen-track set with an interactive world attached. The guest list is loud: Denzel Curry, BIA, SleazyWorld Go, Doe Boy, Babyfxce E, Baby Kia. But the world is the achievement and the records read as evidence for it, which is the wrong way round. OSSHLAND, the debut all sixteen tracks point at, is still unreleased.

entries.name: Karst — Tim Exile
entries.benchmark: creator-ai-tools lane, nearest is Koala Sampler, which shipped small and then stayed shipped
entries.read: In April he shipped a modular system built on Reaktor. On July 28 he discontinued it and sold its replacement. Karst is Tim Exile leaving Native Instruments entirely: a node-based environment that autoconnects without cables, gives every instrument a generative DNA that passes clocks and triggers downstream, and folds composition and performance into the patching rather than treating them as the next step. He made the backers whole, which matters. What they got for it is version 0.1, browser-only, cloud-saved, at £69 against a £99 list, with the standalone and the plugin promised for the fourth quarter and new instruments arriving weekly. The instinct is right and the ledger is thin: two systems in four months, one of them already retired.

entries.name: Surf7 — GOOSE COAT
entries.benchmark: underground-rap lane, nearest is Showly; the difference is an audience built one release at a time
entries.read: Philadelphia decided this one. GOOSE COAT, self-released on June 4 with Surf7 holding both the copyright and the phonogram, has 3.09 million Spotify plays; his next-best song has 252,000. Meek Mill came for the remix on July 24 over a Beatsbyjxckk beat, and that version sits at 161,000. A city legend cosigning a hit is not the same thing as a second record.

issues.forecast: Seattle, Recife, Accra. Nothing on this board is new, and that is the read: a twelve-track album written, produced, mixed, mastered and cover-drawn by one man in one room; a first feature arriving five years after the short that announced it; a first retail sneaker twelve years after four friends started posting outfits. Tenure over arrival.
come_up: Author-of-everything credits: written, produced, mixed, mastered, sleeve, one name
Recife as a production center rather than a location: the door Kleber Mendonca Filho left open
Programs that hand a teenager a camera and a stipend, then hang the results for seven months
decline: The debut read as a beginning rather than a receipt for the decade behind it
Two Jumpman silhouettes in five months standing in for a collection
Campaign photography outrunning the body of work it is meant to introduce
issues.climate: Tenure over arrival. Every object here is somebody's tenth or twelfth or twenty-fifth year, and the useful question is whether the long build shows in the thing itself. AJ Suede has released at pace for a decade and Atomic Justice is the first record where the free association resolves into argument; he handles the boards, the mix, the master and the sleeve. Matheus Farias and Enock Carvalho have worked together thirteen years and sold international rights to their debut before a single public screening. The Studio Museum has run Expanding the Walls since 2001 and hangs seventeen teenagers beside James Van Der Zee. Contemporary Craft gave its main gallery to three artists whose subject is the labor nobody photographs. Against that, Free The Youth put Ghana's eagle on an Air Jordan 16 today and already has a second Jumpman silhouette booked for December, which is a distribution deal moving faster than a catalog can.

entries.name: AJ Suede — Atomic Justice
entries.benchmark: Chris Crack — the same one-man authorship run at volume, though Suede does the boards as well as the bars
entries.read: Written, produced, mixed and mastered by one man in a small room in Seattle, with the sleeve credited to the same name. Atomic Justice went up on Bandcamp on July 14: twelve tracks, no label line, features held to three. Suede has released at this pace for a decade and the early records ran on free association, one image handing off to the next inside a single bar. The writing here is linear, and that is the change worth naming. On “Able to Be Kane” he notices that the cruellest comments tend to arrive from accounts with scripture in the bio, then leaves the observation alone rather than closing it with a punchline. The production stays overcast throughout: a thudding low end under “Billed Gates”, a piano on “Lifting Gravity” that creeps instead of swelling. The detail that decides it: a rapper who could buy beats for a record this considered, and doesn’t. A vinyl LP and a print are the only physical objects attached. No single, no rollout, no announcement post filed a quarter ahead of the thing itself.

entries.name: The Riverbank — Matheus Farias & Enock Carvalho
entries.benchmark: Black Film Archive — nearest on the 50 by root, though the 50 carries no film lane and that is the honest distance
entries.read: Five years after Inabitável played Sundance, Matheus Farias and Enock Carvalho have a first feature, and it goes straight into Locarno’s international competition as a world premiere. A Margem do Rio follows a young Black gay man and former evangelical through Recife, and the pair move it between erotic thriller, tropical noir and something closer to magical realism rather than settling on one. Premium Films and MPM Premium took international sales this week, before a public screening exists to sell. Farias and Carvalho have been partners professionally and privately for thirteen years. Recife did the rest: a decade of work out of Pernambuco made the city legible to programmers, and this is the first debut to walk through that door. Screens 5 to August 15.

entries.name: Through Motion and Repose: Expanding the Walls 2026
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club — the same instinct, a syllabus treated as the artwork and run for years without a launch
entries.read: 144 West 125th Street, up through January 31, 2027. Seventeen teenagers from Manhattan, the Bronx and Queens spent eight months inside the Studio Museum three days a week, worked through the James Van Der Zee archive alongside Dawoud Bey and Carrie Mae Weems, and now hang in the same rooms as Van Der Zee’s prints. Each leaves with a digital camera and a stipend; the program is free and has run since 2001. Christopher Soriano’s Suits at the Corner is a 16 by 20 chromogenic print of men on a street corner, shot close. Nobody here is building a career yet, which is exactly why the pictures are unhurried.

entries.name: Revolutionary Care — Contemporary Craft
entries.benchmark: Project a Black Planet — the nearest thing on the 50 in kind: an argument made in objects rather than wall text
entries.read: Amber Doe, Bekezela Mguni and Alisha B Wormsley, Main Gallery, 5645 Butler Street, Pittsburgh, free, to September 5. Wormsley projects a 22-minute film onto handwoven textiles cut to African American quilting patterns; it was shot across Oakland, Tucson and West Virginia. Mguni spent twenty years organizing before she was a name on a wall, and makes books. The show runs in partnership with Sibyls Shrine, a Pittsburgh network of Black artists who mother.

entries.name: Free The Youth × Air Jordan 16
entries.benchmark: Corteiz — the exact neighbour: a collective that built its own release apparatus first and made the swoosh come to it
entries.read: Four friends started Free The Youth in Accra in 2014 to give Ghanaian creative work somewhere to be seen, and twelve years on they have put the national eagle on the shroud of an Air Jordan 16, a Wilson Smith III silhouette from 2001 that Jordan Brand has barely touched since. Part of the money goes to youth-led projects and grants for Accra designers. Then the arithmetic: pairs go up today at $255 through FTY’s own channels, wider on SNKRS on August 15, and a Free The Youth Air Jordan 3 is already booked for December. Two Jumpman silhouettes inside five months is a distribution deal doing the work a collection should be doing, and the attention is landing on the shroud rather than on the twelve years. Come back when the next object out of Accra is one they made end to end.

issues.forecast: Cardi B previewed a record on a beach on Monday and shipped it on Friday; Ken Carson's tape ran three weeks late and the wait only raised the price. The rollout has become the object. Everything else on this board was made slowly: a novel ten years in the writing, a wardrobe built out of a dead man's photo archive, forty pieces priced from £9.
come_up: Archive as garment — Marathon's Prolific
Kreyòl on a Knopf jacket
Auteur design at homeware prices
decline: The album as the unit — companion tapes are the format now
The announced release date
Streetwear with no document behind it
issues.climate: Rollout over release. The two loudest objects of the week are a four-day single campaign and an eleven-track companion tape that was late because the files missed the streaming deadline, and in both cases the story of the arrival is doing more work than the thing that arrived. The counterweight is documentation. Marathon Clothing's Prolific is the first Nipsey Hussle line built entirely from archive photography, launched three weeks ahead of the posthumous album it is named for. Edwidge Danticat took ten years and 256 pages and titled the book in Kreyòl. Yinka Ilori spent his research budget on Leicester's textile history and put the result in a homeware chain at £9 entry. Where the week is honest, the object outlives the week it was announced in.

entries.name: Dèy — Edwidge Danticat
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club — the 50's literature lane, and this is the shelf it exists for
entries.read: Magnolia hears gunfire in a Miami shopping mall, takes cover in a restaurant with strangers, gets home safely and tells nobody. That silence is the engine of Edwidge Danticat's first novel in ten years. The title is Haitian Kreyòl for mourning and the book does not stage it. What surviving the afternoon gives Magnolia is clear sight of everything she had been managing not to look at: her daughter Zoë, the child's father, a mother whose unraveling she can feel starting in her own hands, a father with a second family, and Haiti underneath all of it, where her parents and her sibling absorb losses on the ordinary weekday scale. Danticat has been publishing since Breath, Eyes, Memory in 1994 and has never needed a plot to carry her. She needs a sentence. Hannah Jocelyn picked the book in The New Yorker on sentences alone; Publishers Weekly starred it; Kirkus reads it as a study of motherhood, nationhood and violence. Ten years is a long time to hold a novel back. Check on August 25 whether one afternoon in a Florida mall can hold a decade of Haiti inside it. Publishes August 25 by Knopf — 256 pages, $30, with a seven-hour audiobook read by Melinda Sewak.

entries.name: Prolific — The Marathon Clothing
entries.benchmark: Denim Tears — the same move, an archive used as the print rather than a graphic laid on top
entries.read: Every piece in this line carries a photograph, and that is the whole design brief. Prolific launched on July 27 through The Marathon Clothing, the company Nipsey Hussle founded, and it is the first collection built entirely from his archive: heavyweight tees, long sleeves, hoodies, crewnecks, zip-ups, hats, with handwritten graphics and his own typography. The 'All Summer' shirt prints lyrics from 'Who Detached Us,' a 2011 record. Earlier Marathon drops were streetwear with a logo attached; this is a wardrobe assembled as documentation, which is a harder object for an estate to get right than a memorial tee. It arrives three weeks before the album of the same name, fifteen tracks with Bino Rideaux, digital on August 14 with vinyl and cassette to follow. Seven years after Crenshaw, the ownership argument is still the clearest one anybody in rap has made.

entries.name: Yinka Ilori × Dunelm
entries.benchmark: Lauren Halsey — public-facing, community-sourced, color used as an argument rather than a finish
entries.read: A £9 cotton hand towel and a £799 bouclé ottoman bed, same signature, same shop. Yinka Ilori's forty-piece collection for Dunelm landed on July 8 across furniture, bedding, lighting, rugs and soft furnishings: the 'Sweet Flows' swivel chair at £299, the 'Bell' dimmable lamp at £65, the 'Half-Log' sideboard at £599 in oak on chrome legs. The research underneath it is real. Dunelm began as a market stall in Leicester, and the florals across the range are drawn from national flowers of India, Pakistan and elsewhere, tracing the Asian, African and Caribbean communities who built the city's textile trade last century. The campaign was shot with actual Dunelm staff. What thins is the translation: printed jacquard at chain-store volume flattens a practice that normally works in three dimensions and outdoors. The strongest object is the quietest one, the handmade 'Kaleidoscope' rug in 100 per cent wool from £135. Check in a year whether any of it is still stocked.

entries.name: Cardi B — Ah Ha
entries.benchmark: Jim Legxacy — the nearest thing on the 50, and the distance is scale against specificity
entries.read: Monday she rapped it walking a beach in a Dominican flag bikini; Wednesday Atlantic set the date; Friday it was out. Four days, and the phone clip did the work a campaign used to do. 'Ah Ha' is a club record that knows exactly what it is, and her first solo release since Am I the Drama? in September 2025. Nothing behind it has been announced. Come back when there is an album date.

entries.name: Ken Carson — cartunez
entries.benchmark: Chris Crack — releases at the same pace and edits harder for it
entries.read: Eleven tracks, four weeks after a 22-track album, from a rapper whose More Chaos took the Billboard 200 in April 2025 on 59,500 units. The engine is real: Carson built the live show before the catalog, and Opium is one of the few complete visual worlds operating at this scale. cartunez was due on July 10 and missed it because the files did not reach streaming in time, which turned three dead weeks into the loudest stretch of the rollout. Merch was circulating on Nettspend, OsamaSon and Apollo Red while nothing shipped. The tape extends where it could have argued, and he headlines ComplexCon in October regardless. Come back when a Ken Carson release is a record rather than a companion.

issues.forecast: Nothing on this board was settled by a rollout. The week's real argument is about who gets to hold things: a Benin City museum with a finished building and a revoked land title, a sculptor welding in the tradition of the guild families whose plaques are still coming home, a Kingston novel that keeps a 1988 attack on the record. Custody over release.
come_up: Rammed earth as civic architecture
The 1980s Caribbean back on the record
Devotional painting priced below its museum footprint
decline: The guest list as the marketing plan
Opening dates announced before consent is settled
Stream counts standing in for a catalog
issues.climate: Custody over release. Every object here is a claim on something somebody else would rather administer. MOWAA's Institute is built, 4,500 square meters of rammed earth, and the Edo State government revoked its certificate of occupancy; the museum now opens by appointment. Favour Jonathan welds in a lineage she traces to the Idumwun-igun-nugboha families on Sakpomba Road, and showed this spring in an exhibition founded on a Dutch museum handing its plaque back to the Oba. Marlon James spent his sixth novel on eight men in a Kingston rehearsal room in 1988 and on what the survivors did after the mob. Gustavo Nazareno framed twenty-four paintings as an offering to a deity rather than a collection for a fair. Against that, MOLIY put out twelve tracks in thirty-two minutes with nine guests on them, three months after a remix cleared a billion streams. The room found her first. What she keeps once the summer ends is the open question.

entries.name: How to Grow a Flower from a Supernova — Gustavo Nazareno
entries.benchmark: Project a Black Planet — the 50's diaspora-thesis lane, and Nazareno is that argument held in one hand
entries.read: Twenty-four paintings and ten charcoal drawings, hung at Opera Gallery Paris across Haute Couture Week and framed not as a collection but as an offering to Pomba Gira, the Candomblé deity of beauty, seduction and transformation. Nazareno grinds charcoal to dust and builds blacks that keep their detail where oil would flatten; his figures wear garments borrowed from the vocabulary of McQueen and Galliano until the cloth stops behaving like clothing and becomes weather, landscape, veil. He told the gallery the title came from reading about Betelgeuse, and the thought that the star might explode inside his lifetime and be visible from here. Born 1994, studio in São Paulo, family rooted in Umbanda, which is where he says the work started. The institutional record is already long: Museu Afro Brasil in 2023, MAMAM in Recife in 2024, One Becomes Many at the Pérez in Miami, and UNBOUND at the Museum of the African Diaspora in San Francisco, which runs to August 16. His auction record is $6,985. The gap is that the museums arrived before the market did, which is the correct order and almost never the actual one.

entries.name: The Disappearers — Marlon James
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club — the 50's reading lane, and this is a shelf entry rather than a season pick
entries.read: Kingston, 1988. Eight men who are strangers to one another start rehearsing a play, and the only thing they hold in common is that all of them are gay. A mob finds them. One dies. James gives his sixth novel to what the survivors do next, which is where it gets hard: some chase retribution, some vanish, some decide nothing happened. Booker longlisted on July 28, his third nomination. The room is correct.

entries.name: Favour Jonathan
entries.benchmark: Lauren Halsey — the 50's public-monument lane, and the nearest neighbour by method as much as subject
entries.read: She welds. The pieces come together as patchwork metal, sparks flying, in a practice she traces to the Idumwun-igun-nugboha guild families on Sakpomba Road in Benin City, where she grew up. Her Central Saint Martins degree piece, Ododo and Divinity, a standing female figure with a leopard, went into the school's permanent archive. In 2022 she built a fourteen-meter public sculpture of Ira Aldridge for the National Collection Center in Coventry, and a memorial to Claudia Jones at the Black Cultural Archives in Brixton. This spring she was one of ten Edo artists in Back to Benin at Museum de Fundatie in Zwolle, an exhibition whose founding act was the museum returning its only Benin plaque to Oba Ewuare II in November 2025. Public commissions at that scale, an archive acquisition, and still no gallery representation.

entries.name: MOWAA Institute — Museum of West African Art
entries.benchmark: The Shed — the 50's places lane, and the comparison is about civic ambition, not scale
entries.read: The building is the real thing. Four and a half thousand square meters of locally sourced rammed earth under an in-situ concrete roof, with conservation labs, material science labs and a hundred-seat auditorium, laid out from the spatial logic of Benin City's own earthworks. Adjaye calls it Nigerian modernism and for once the phrase earns itself. Then the politics: protesters broke into the preview on November 9, 2025, the Edo State governor revoked the certificate of occupancy, and the palace disputed the museum's account of its own name. Roughly £40m, with the Getty Foundation, Open Society and the British Museum among the funders. It opens by appointment. Come back when the Oba, the state and the trustees have signed the same piece of paper.

entries.name: BADDIES <3 MOLIY — MOLIY
entries.benchmark: Victony — the 50's global-diaspora lane, and the comparison is unflattering on ownership, not on talent
entries.read: The hooks survive four continents, and this is the proof of it: twelve tracks, thirty-two minutes, Tyla, Shenseea, Skillibeng, Sarkodie and Yailin La Más Viral spread across them, with ACCRA GIRLS the best thing on the record. MOLIY came up in alté, which is where the interesting Ghanaian-American writing has sat for a decade. The Shake It To The Max remix cleared a billion streams and gamma signed the moment it made. What arrived is a thirty-two-minute project carrying nine guests, which is a compilation more than a catalog. Victony answered the same question by putting SLICK out on his own imprint and filling it himself. Come back when there is a MOLIY album with three features and forty minutes on it.

issues.forecast: A jewelry film shot in Kerala this summer opens by refusing to be admired and ends with lemons and chilies worn as armor. That is the week's shape. Four of these five are arguments about who is holding the camera and who is standing in front of it, and the fifth is a Miami scene taking its own sound back off the people who exported it. The lens over the subject.
come_up: Self-funded documentary out of Lagos
Protective charms worn as jewelry
Miami phonk originators back on record
decline: Culture treated as a series of chapters
The bridal script in jewelry advertising
Credit that arrives a decade late
issues.climate: The lens over the subject. Deborah Willis built the Mississippi show on a claim she states without hedging, that self-representation is power, and the rest of the board is that claim tested in four directions. Niyi Fagbemi funds his own trips and says so plainly; the Ojude Oba film nobody paid for cleared a hundred million views and pulled an Ijebu-Ode festival onto the international calendar. Bhavya Ramesh and NorBlack NorWhite took the nazar battu off the doorway and put it on the body, then built the campaign around being watched rather than admired. SpaceGhostPurrp invented a genre that circled the world without him and is back on a record with Robb Bank$ on August 7. James Fenwick flies in with a crew, shoots other people's traditions beautifully, credits the local choreographers, and calls the series Born From Culture. Whose culture is the question the series has not answered yet.

entries.name: Photography and the Black Arts Movement, 1955–1985
entries.benchmark: Black Film Archive — the 50's editorial-taste lane, and the same instinct applied to the still image
entries.read: Around a hundred and fifty works, over a hundred artists, and a thesis stated without hedging: self-representation is power. Deborah Willis and Philip Brookman built it for the National Gallery, it ran at the Getty through June, and its last stop is the Mississippi Museum of Art until November 8. Dawoud Bey, Kwame Brathwaite, Roy DeCarava, Gordon Parks, Ming Smith, Malick Sidibé, Jamel Shabazz, Carrie Mae Weems, Lorna Simpson. The Jackson presentation is the reason to care about the last stop rather than the first: MMA partnered with Jackson State's Margaret Walker Center, which runs the COFO Learning Center, and hung rarely seen photographs from the 1973 Phillis Wheatley Poetry Festival with Audre Lorde, Alice Walker, Sonia Sanchez and Nikki Giovanni in one room. Mississippi photographers Doris Derby and Roy Lewis are in the activism section with their own wall labels. A touring show usually loses something at each stop. This one arrived home and got heavier.

entries.name: RB$GP — Robb Bank$ & SpaceGhostPurrp
entries.benchmark: Starlito — the 50's underground-rap lane, the regional lifer who never took the exit
entries.read: BANG DEN is the video, RB$GP is the album, and it lands August 7. Purrp started Raider Klan in Miami Gardens in 2008, ran Denzel Curry, Xavier Wulf, Chris Travis, Pouya and Yung Simmie through it, coined phonk, and then watched the genre circle the planet on other people's uploads while the Klan folded in 2015. Robb Bank$ is Shaggy's son, estranged, out of Broward, and the one alumnus who never stopped making the sound. Two men from the same collapsed scene, one of whom wrote the template that half a streaming category now runs on. Phonk sells more smoothly when the man who named it stays a rumor, and nobody currently billing against it has any reason to correct that. He made a record instead.

entries.name: STARE — Bhavya Ramesh × NorBlack NorWhite
entries.benchmark: Denim Tears — the 50's diasporic-fashion lane, history carried on the body rather than printed about
entries.read: Thirteen pieces in silver and gold, built out of the nazar battu, the lemon-and-chilli charm that hangs outside Indian homes against the evil eye. Eyes, snakes, fangs, moons, ghungroos. The film, directed by Bijoy Shetty in Kerala with Tillotama Shome and Karthika Nair, is folk horror rather than a wedding. Indian jewelry advertising has run the same script for thirty years, and it casts the woman as the person the jewelry is given to. This one casts her as the one doing the looking.

entries.name: Niyi Fagbemi
entries.benchmark: Monocle — the 50's editorial-taste lane, and the difference is that Monocle is a business
entries.read: Ninety-nine percent of what he shoots is self-funded and he says it in interviews without softening it. Nobody commissioned the 2023 Ojude Oba film. It cleared a hundred million views across platforms and turned an Ijebu-Ode festival into a fixture with an international attendance problem. He trained as a mechanical engineer at Covenant, borrowed his uncle's camera in third year, and now shoots the Durbar in Kano, Juju Rock in Niger State, Ibadan's brown roofs. Naija In Motion, his first solo exhibition, opened in Lagos last October, and every print was hung in its natural color with no manipulation, which is a position rather than a preference. He also names the limits out loud: funding first, then security, and the places he will not travel to because of it.

entries.name: Born From Culture — James Mitchal Fenwick
entries.benchmark: Project a Black Planet — the 50's diaspora-thesis lane, and that one is argued from inside
entries.read: The Georgia chapter is properly made. Eighty dancers from the Apkhazeti Ensemble at the Chronicle of Georgia, choreography by Bachana Chanturia, shot in 67km/h winds across three costume changes, and it looks like nothing else in that feed. The Aotearoa chapter followed last month, built on haka, waiata and whakapapa. Fenwick credits the ensembles and the choreographers by name, which is more than most people who fly in do. But the tagline is ancient tradition, modern eyes, and the eyes are always his. A format that treats each culture as the next chapter will eventually spend the thing that made the first one good. Come back when a chapter is directed by someone from the place it is about.

issues.forecast: The two people who wrote most of the best British soul album of the last three years spent this July putting out their own. DAMEDAME* are from Walsall, they wrote and produced the bulk of Jorja Smith's Falling or Flying, and DREAMS ON THE PASSENGER SEAT runs twenty-seven minutes. Everything below sorts on one axis: who has a body of work out, and who is still living off a single. The body over the single.
come_up: Writer-producers releasing under their own names
The Black Country as its own sound center
Twenty-seven-minute albums that finish their argument
decline: The cosign standing in for a catalog
Debut albums due 'later this year,' every year
Festival billing outrunning the release schedule
issues.climate: The body over the single. British R&B has never had a deeper bench of writers and producers, and for most of the last decade the arrangement was that they stayed behind the glass while somebody else fronted the record. That arrangement is being renegotiated in public. Barbara Boko and Edith Nelson wrote and produced the bulk of Falling or Flying and produced on Jim Legxacy's black british music (2025); their own debut landed on July 24 with almost no campaign attached. Nia Smith answered a 2024 debut EP with a second one on May 29 and collected a MOBO Best Newcomer nomination for it. Against that, Tamera has thirteen and a half million plays on a single from 2021 and a debut album that has been arriving 'later this year' for three years running, and Finn Askew has cosigns from SZA, Kehlani and Bieber attached to a seventeen-minute tape. Legxacy is the exception that proves the rule: one new single in the twelve months since BBM, and a festival summer running entirely on a record that came out last July. The room will hold a position on a catalog. It will not hold one on a promise.

entries.name: Jim Legxacy
entries.benchmark: Jim Legxacy is already the 50's underground-rap anchor; Starlito and Chris Crack are the lane he sets the line for
entries.read: Lollapalooza yesterday, Golden Gate Park on the ninth, Victoria Park on the twenty-ninth. The billing is the size of a second album and there isn't one yet. black british music (2025) came out on XL on July 18 last year, entered the UK chart at 29 and then outlived most of what sat above it; three BRIT nominations and four MOBO nods followed. Since then, one new single — 'idk idk,' built on a soul loop he produced himself, Natanya on the harmonies. The room is loud and the room is correct. On the follow-up, he already answered: when he dropped 'idk idk' he said the next one would take him some time. He's earned it.

entries.name: DREAMS ON THE PASSENGER SEAT — DAMEDAME*
entries.benchmark: Jim Legxacy — they produced on black british music (2025), and this is the 50's clearest case of the room hearing the writers years before it hears the artists
entries.read: The bulk of Jorja Smith's Falling or Flying was written and produced by two women from Walsall, which is also where Smith is from, and for three years that was most of the public record on Barbara Boko and Edith Nelson. DREAMS ON THE PASSENGER SEAT changes it. Ten songs, twenty-seven minutes and thirty-two seconds, out July 24 on Robots & Humans through Sony UK, and it is the rare producer-to-artist move that does not sound like a demo reel. The instrumentation is played rather than stacked: strings carrying an actual arrangement, basslines that sit off the beat and stay there, transatlantic soul read through UK jazz instead of borrowed wholesale from Atlanta. They debuted as an act in 2023 with 'A STRANGER,' which EA picked up for FC24, and have since produced for Calvin Harris, Tems, Wizkid and Jim Legxacy. The subject matter stays domestic. Somebody cooks for you. Somebody refuses to answer the question. The sadness that never makes it to the story. The gap is that they have been among the most consequential people in British soul for three years and this is the first record with their name at the top of it.

entries.name: Payback Is A Dog — Nia Smith
entries.benchmark: Baby Rose — the 50's soul-voice lane, with a Brixton and Kingston accent on it
entries.read: 'I'm kind of exhausted at the moment,' she told NME from Brixton, a week short of her birthday and a month after Payback Is A Dog landed on May 29 via 0207 Def Jam. The exhaustion is earned. Jools Holland, Glastonbury, a Popcaan remix, an Ivor Novello Rising Star nomination, a MOBO Best Newcomer nod, and an invitation from Prada to Milan. Second EP, second time the room was right.

entries.name: Tamera
entries.benchmark: Victony — the 50's global-diaspora lane; the same Afro-R&B crossing from the other side of the Atlantic
entries.read: 'Wickedest' is five years old and still turning over thirteen and a half million plays, which is what a well-written song does. Tamera Cuthbert left Gravesend for London in 2017, made Afrodite in 2021 with P2J on the boards, followed it with L.I.T (Lost in Translation) in 2023, and has spent this year in a generous run of singles: 'Blessings,' 'Helpless,' 'Sinner,' then 'Undeniable' with Aitch in May.
